atom_reviews.question: Are there any elephants in the image?
atom_reviews.expert_evidence: Fine-grained classifier Top-1: African elephant (logit 8.34); Indian elephant ranked 3rd (logit 5.52). Router verdicts: Twin-domed skull=False, Small ears=False, Single finger trunk=False, Arched back=False. Only generic proboscidean traits (massive body, wrinkled skin, tail tuft) are present.
atom_reviews.reasoning: Binary presence is satisfied, but species-level taxonomy fails catastrophically. The prompt specified Indian elephant; the image shows definitive African elephant morphology (large fan-shaped ears, single dome, concave back, long tusks). This is not a minor attribute error but a complete class mismatch. Taxonomy score reduced to 0.2 to reflect that only ~20% of diagnostic checkpoints (generic body/skin/tail) are met while all species-defining features are absent.

authenticity_review: High photorealism overall with natural lighting and texture. Two minor structural artifacts noted: (1) rear-right elephant's hind legs show slight fusion with reeds and adjacent elephant leg, and (2) water-leg interface lacks realistic refraction/displacement, appearing painted-on. These are severity-2 issues that reduce authenticity from perfect but do not indicate systemic failure. Perceptual quality auditor reported no graphics-level distortions.
